The health service running in random networks may take you by surprise, but don't let that deter you from playing this game. "Bit" invites us to uncover their story, and the imaginary world they inhabit is fascinating. While some players might find the gameplay repetitive after using each tool at least once, those who enjoy exploring hypothetical networks to discover vulnerabilities using imaginative tools will find this game rewarding.

There are a few additions that I think would have made this game even better:
- It would be beneficial to include a coding feature in the game that allows players to create their own imaginary exploits and or fix the exploits they find on random servers.
- The multiplayer that the Developer mentions post-game, where players can defend against incoming attacks and trace them to launch counterattacks, sounds like an exciting addition to the game.
- Including the Healthcare Services running on random networks late game would not make sense as it was only introduced for a specific mission. It is unlikely for a company to run this type of service. Instead, adding a wider range of services running on various ports would be a more realistic way to make the game's infrastructures feel authentic and increase the game's level of difficulty.
- It would be great if the game had more severe consequences for leaving behind logs or other traces. Additionally, it would be interesting if there were an achievement for successfully completing the game without leaving any traces behind.
- Additional side quests like one before joining Entropy. I came across a text file in the game that asked for help. Initially, I struggled to figure out how to create a text file, but eventually, I managed to do so. I followed the instructions in the text file and placed my message in a new text file next to it. Despite my efforts, nothing happened after that.
- An option in the Network View Sorter executable to move unnecessary nodes away from frequently accessed ones like questing and asset servers, and current mission objectives.

Fun game, neat story, recommend with DLC for complete experience ([spoiler]this one even includes a small counter hack that you have to do on your actual real machine, outside the game that acts as your VM)[/spoiler]. 'Gotta go fast' isn't necessarily the best way to play this, I recommend trying to search every corner in the terminals you connect to, go hunt and read all (or most) the information you can get, as in some cases that will unlock some potential new interesting challenges that you could miss. Obviously, this is miles away from being completely accurate real life hacking, but if it was then you would have months (or even years) of "funny" attempts ending in failure ahead of you. It's meant to be a game that includes some accurate aspects though (just don't go thinking you could go completely untraceable by only deleting the files in the log folder in a real scenario, but it's still an accurate introductory concept).
 
Developers should consider creating a HackNet 2 that explores and adds more on the concepts already present in this game.

Total Score = 58/100.

GAMEPLAY:
The game simulates a Unix-like operating system, with every main element of the game's interface having its own window. The main gameplay is done through two large interfaces, a graphical display, and a Unix terminal. Both interfaces are essential for gameplay, though the player can use either as their "main" interface. Along with the terminal, the computers in the game simulate a Unix-like file system, through which the player can explore the computer, and even destroy them by deleting critical system files. 

The core of the gameplay is to connect to other computers and run dedicated programs to break the security and acquire superuser privileges on the computer. Each program takes up a certain amount of memory, which the player has to manage, as there is only a limited amount of memory to share.

Games pretty fun if you're into hacking and cybersecurity. It's not a 1:1 for hacking though so if you're expecting to rely on this game entirely for your cybersecurity education then you'll be wasting your time. 
It gets navigating a linux filesystem right, but you won't be hacking ssh ports open in real life just to name a few examples. 
Overall, its a great game with an interesting story and some really fun and intense moments. (looking at you Naix)

P.S. If you wanna learn real hacking then hop on over to TryHackMe.com or HackTheBox.com to get started.
